children: The current strength of U.S. steel spreads are cementing Jefferies's bullish stance toward BlueScope Steel. Jefferies expects Bluescope to achieve 1H Ebit of A$960 million. That's at the top end of BlueScope's A$860 million-A$960 million guidance. "We see further upgrade risk for 2H27 given spot of US$890/ton and consensus assuming US$650/ton," analyst Ramoun Lazar says. Jefferies has penciled in US$700/ton for 2H. "Bluescope remains attractive on 8% FY27 free cash flow yield, supporting more than A$1 billion shareholder returns per annum," Jefferies adds. It retains a buy call and A$40.00/share price target. BlueScope ended Tuesday at A$32.83. (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)
